solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Note slippery patch on road: that is expected in December

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: sol (soh) is a note of the sol-fa scale
ST is the abbreviation for street, a road
ice is a slippery patch on a road

explanation.surface: A warning that black ice on the roads is to be expected in December.
explanation.definitionFit: The winter solstice falls around 21 December, the shortest day of the year in the north.

clue.text: Deprived of stone, created statue without head

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds

indicators.note: without head means its first letter is removed

parts.note: to create a statue is to carve one, so carved

explanation.surface: A sculptor deprived of stone carved a statue missing its head.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight of 14 pounds, written ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Starved of something means deprived of it, as in starved of attention.

clue.text: One's fired up here to hold flat-warming party?

definitions.meaning: a rocket is fired upwards from a ...
to launch a pad, celebrating a new flat, which is slang pad

explanation.surface: A rocket fired up from where someone is about to throw a housewarming.
explanation.walkthrough: Pad is slang for a flat, so launching a pad is a playful take on a flat-warming party.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch pad is the platform rockets lift off from, and a pad is informal for a home.

clue.text: Many turning up old doctor injected, chancy business

indicators.note: the old and doctor pieces are injected inside, placed within
in a down entry, turning up reads the word from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a lot means many
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A lot of people turn up for an old doctor's injections, a risky business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses A LOT to TOLA; 'injected' puts O and MB inside after its T. A tombola is a British raffle drawing tickets from a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a lottery at a fete, a game of chance.

clue.text: Wow: lovely piece of plasterwork

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like wow
nice means lovely

explanation.surface: Someone admiring a fine bit of ornamental plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor is a British slang exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornice is a decorative plaster moulding running round a ceiling.

clue.text: European power in tricky situation, trying to hold this?

indicators.note: the power piece goes in the tricky situation, placed inside it

parts.note: a mire is a difficult situation, a mess
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A European power in a tight spot, struggling to keep hold of its overseas territories.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back through the whole clue: what a European power in trouble was trying to keep.
explanation.definitionFit: European powers in decline struggled to keep their colonial empires, the territories they ruled abroad.

clue.text: Largely excused, lolled around rear of bar: perfect

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, its last letter cut

parts.note: exempt means excused from a duty

indicators.note: the lolled piece goes around the other letter

parts.note: lay is the past tense of lie, to loll

indicators.note: rear of means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone mostly let off, lounging at the back of the bar, which is perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' drops the final T; 'around' wraps the lolling word round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Exemplary means serving as a model, faultless, as in exemplary behaviour.

clue.text: Work over, provided with a dish of porridge

indicators.note: over means the word is turned over, reversed

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
lent means provided or supplied

explanation.surface: Once the work is over, someone is given a bowl of porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Polenta is an Italian dish of boiled cornmeal, a kind of porridge.

clue.text: Rough treatment in battles over wood

indicators.note: over means the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: war is battles collectively
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Harsh treatment in wartime fighting over timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw deal is unfair treatment, rough handling from fate or others.

clue.text: By virtue of being fighting man, following a colour

indicators.note: the pieces come after the letter a

parts.note: qua is Latin-derived English for 'in the capacity of'
a marine is a soldier serving with a navy

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a colour simply because they are a fighting man following another.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquamarine is a pale blue-green shade, named after the gemstone.

clue.text: Have a home not left to turn dirty

indicators.note: turning the remaining letters means reading them backwards
not left means the letter for left is dropped from the word

parts.note: to dwell is to live somewhere, have a home

explanation.surface: Someone without a home, not even a left-luggage spot, is turning to dirty ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd and dirty are both used of crude, smutty jokes or behaviour.

clue.text: Something for tea — Veronica's to pig out

indicators.note: out means the letters of these words are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: At tea time Veronica is going to gorge herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges VERONICASTOPIG, all fourteen letters of the fodder, apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victoria sponge is a jam-filled sponge cake, a classic of the British afternoon tea table.

clue.text: Corrupt record separates Democrat from party

indicators.note: the record sits between the other two pieces, keeping them apart

parts.note: a rave is a wild party
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A political scandal in which a recorded tape divides a Democrat from his party.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprave is to corrupt morally, to lead someone into wickedness.

clue.text: Make fresher talent vie to be broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A talent show where contestants compete on air to freshen things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To ventilate a room is to let fresh air in, making it fresher.

clue.text: Staff given a hint: uniform is missing cuff

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it

indicators.note: the hint lacks the uniform letter, so it is taken out

parts.note: a clue is a hint
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Staff are tipped off that a uniform is missing a cuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuff' looks like part of a uniform, but it is the definition in its handcuff sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A manacle is a metal shackle for the wrist, and cuff is short for handcuff.

clue.text: Firm turning off current to make wiring safe for government office

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: turning off the current means removing its letter from the word

parts.note: insulate means wrap wires to make them safe
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An electrical firm switching off the power to make the wiring safe at a government building.
explanation.definitionFit: A consulate is the office of a consul, an official representing a foreign government.

clue.text: Moving awkwardly after dispatching large cotton sheets

indicators.note: dispatching the large letter means removing it from the word

parts.note: waddling is walking with a clumsy rocking gait
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Someone moving clumsily after sending off large cotton sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Wadding is soft cotton padding sold in sheets for stuffing and lining.

clue.text: Essayist is to have another boy

parts.note: to have more of something is to add it, as in add to the family
another is one more, and I is the roman numeral one
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An essayist announcing that the family is expecting another son.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as ADD I SON, add one son, which is what having another boy means; 'is' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison was the 18th-century writer of essays for The Spectator and The Tatler.

clue.text: Make weird changes, even more unstylish

parts.note: to do is to make, as in do a drawing

indicators.note: changes means the letters of weird are rearranged

explanation.surface: Making weird alterations to clothes leaves them even less stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowdy describes drab, unfashionable dress, so dowdier is still more unstylish.

clue.text: Enemy agents quietly dropped next to a shrub

indicators.note: the quiet letter is taken out of the spy ring

parts.note: a spy ring is a network of enemy agents
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Enemy agents silently drop something next to a bush as a dead-letter drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Syringa is the botanical genus of lilac, also used for the mock orange bush.

clue.text: Bookish type succeeded, anger being expressed

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

indicators.note: being expressed means the word is spoken, so its sound is used

parts.note: choler is an old word for anger

explanation.surface: A bookish type who got their way but showed their anger.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person devoted to study and books.

clue.text: Stuff children, offering garlic

parts.note: to ram is to stuff or cram
sons are children

explanation.surface: Someone forcing garlic on their children at mealtimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramsons is wild garlic, a woodland plant with edible leaves.

clue.text: Reach that is very limited by pain

indicators.note: limited by means the pieces are enclosed within the pain word

parts.note: an ache is a pain
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A reach that is badly restricted by pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited by' sets the two short pieces inside the pain word, after its H.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve a goal is to reach it, attain it.

clue.text: Why spitting feathers (blue)?

definitions.meaning: down is fine feathers, so feathers being spat out are cryptically ...

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a person spitting feathers looks so blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spitting feathers' is an idiom for being furious, a false trail; here down is literally feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Down in the mouth is an idiom for looking miserable, which is what feeling blue means.

clue.text: Shortly up and about, I'm sparkling

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: astir means out of bed and moving about

explanation.surface: Someone up and about briefly, declaring they feel full of fizz.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont, so the wine might fairly say it sparkles.

clue.text: Moved a mile to make address better

indicators.note: the letters of the words a mile are moved around into a new order

parts.note: to orate is to address an audience with a speech

explanation.surface: A speaker shifted a mile to give a better address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a verb here, to improve; 'address' is the speaking verb, not a location.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is to improve something, to make it better.

clue.text: Disloyal squad one left with regret

indicators.note: one left means the letter for one has left, removed from the squad

parts.note: a unit is a squad of soldiers
I is the roman numeral one
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A squad member left behind with regret, feeling his comrades were disloyal.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue in the sense of unfaithful, as in a lover proving false.

clue.text: Agree to get involved with Mrs Wordsworth's home

indicators.note: the letters of agree get mixed up with those of Mrs, rearranged together

explanation.surface: Mrs Wordsworth is asked to agree to things at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get involved with' shuffles AGREE and MRS together. Grasmere is a village in England's Lake District where Wordsworth lived at Dove Cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet William Wordsworth lived at Dove Cottage in Grasmere, so it was his home.
